# Actual global-cut response cone and a finite-support alternative

This note uses the paired-support construction proved independently by
root and Slab: finite global supporting-cut erosions of one canonical
fiber family admit actual positive linear combinations of their physical
boundary speeds. Its full geometric proof is in Slab's corresponding
Cartesian-product support-cut source. This note supplies the finite-menu
duality consequence and its exact limits. It does NOT prove a positive
game value or an OC conclusion.

## 1. The geometric operation and its hypotheses

Fix a finite complete base P and positive compatible bodies K_z. Every
action A consists of finitely many continuously u-indexed cuts

 u.x+epsilon V_i(u,z,x)<=ell_i(u,z),   |u|=1,

intersected with the original canonical hull. Here ell_i is affine in z,
continuous and bounded in u, and ell_i(u,z)>=h_(K_z)(u) at every original
base. The field V_i is finite, nonnegative, continuous, and convex in
the full physical variables(z,x). It is enough to have these properties
on a common convex neighborhood of the compact hull. Each action is an
actual nested convex deformation with positive original integer fibers.

Include in EACH action finitely many zero-field cuts ell_p, p in P,
where ell_p(u,p)=h_(K_p)(u) and ell_p dominates all fiber supports. Their
bounded continuous slopes exist by the proved finite-KKT selection. They
do not change any body. At a regular boundary point of fiber z, with
normal u, the action's exact speed is

 v_A(z,x)=max{V_i(u,z,x):ell_i(u,z)=h_(K_z)(u)}.           (1)

The augmented active set is never empty. For N>=1 actions A_1,...,A_N and
coefficients t_j>=0, form all tuples of one cut from each action. For
each tuple choose the baseline and field

 ell_tuple=(1/N)sum_j ell_(j,i_j),
 V_tuple=sum_j t_j V_(j,i_j).                           (2)

The baseline is valid and its slack is the average of nonnegative old
slacks. Its active set therefore consists EXACTLY of tuples of active
old cuts. All new fields are convex and nonnegative. Applying(1) gives

 v_new=max_active tuples sum_j t_j V_(j,i_j)
                         =sum_j t_j v_(A_j).            (3)

The construction uses one finite Cartesian product and then one small
positive epsilon; it is not a limit of bodies or a formal vector sum.
Uniform inner homothets keep every original base positive, so the new
projection equals conv(P) and every anchored inclusion holds exactly.
The nonsmooth radial first-variation theorem applies, including d=1.
All supporting-cap traces below are the actual inward-loss selectors.

## 2. Fixed-cap physical responses really add

Fix m>=1 closed ambient halfspaces H_1,...,H_m and a real beta. Their inward
loss selectors kappa_j(z,x) are one on full/inside supporting traces,
zero on empty/outside supporting traces, and the strict cap indicator
on proper boundary traces. Pure integer closed traces retain their full
or empty value. Define

 D(A)=sum_z int_(boundary K_z) v_A dS,
 C_j(A)=sum_z int kappa_j v_A dS,
 R_j(A)=C_j(A)-beta D(A).                               (4)

All these integrals are finite. Equations(3)--(4) prove exact additivity
of EVERY coordinate(D,C_1,...,C_m), and therefore of the signed vector R.
In particular the response vectors obtainable by all actions in this
class form a convex cone containing zero. Fixed finite lists of actions
have their entire response convex hull realized by actual bodies.

Unlike Minkowski interpolation of eroded bodies, this operation does
not change the cap-response vector through a nonlinear flattening of
facets. Unlike the earlier one-source field-mixture theorem, it permits
different sources, support slopes, contact sets, and existing maxima of
source demands. The addition is implemented by NEW paired baseline cuts.

For a finite action menu A_1,...,A_N, a probability mixture alpha has
physical response sum alpha_i R(A_i). Its attained best guaranteed row is

 max_(alpha in simplex_N) min_j sum_i alpha_i R_j(A_i)
    =min_(lambda in simplex_m) max_i sum_j lambda_j R_j(A_i). (5)

This is finite convex separation of conv{R(A_i)} from an open positive
orthant, as proved in the one-source minimax source. Every value on the
left is a physical first response by(2), not a distribution over candidate
centers or a randomized guarantee.

## 3. An arbitrary action class needs no compactness assumption

Let A be ANY collection of finite actions as above, possibly uncountable
and without compact parameters. Exactly one of the following holds:

 (P) A finite selection A_1,...,A_N and t_i>=0 has
                     sum_i t_i R_j(A_i)>0 for every j.

 (D) There is lambda in simplex_m with
                     sum_j lambda_j R_j(A)<=0 for EVERY A in A. (6)

If(P) holds, the combined body in(2) realizes its strict positive vector.
The two conditions cannot coexist by taking their scalar pairing.
For existence, let C be the convex conic hull of all response vectors.
If(P) fails, C is disjoint from the open positive orthant. Its closure
is also disjoint from that orthant: any point of the closure in this
open set would be approximated by points of C inside it. Separating the
closed cone from the open orthant gives a nonzero functional lambda
which is nonnegative on the positive orthant and nonpositive on C.
Its coordinates are nonnegative; normalize their sum to one. This
proves(D). No closedness of the ORIGINAL response cone is asserted.

Equivalently, if every probability vector lambda admits ONE action A
with lambda.R(A)>0, then(P) holds. A direct finite-selection proof is
also useful: the open sets {lambda:lambda.R(A)>0} cover the compact
simplex. Choose a finite subcover. Its continuous maximum has a strictly
positive minimum, and the finite minimax(5) gives a positive mixture.
Thus only finitely many concrete deformations are ever needed to obtain
a strict descent, despite the absence of a global compact action menu.

Once a positive vector has been found, normalize its coefficients to
sum to one; all strict signs persist. Caratheodory then reduces its
representation to at most m+1 actions while retaining the same response
vector. If D and the m separate cap losses must be preserved as well,
at most m+2 actions suffice. The final epsilon is chosen after this
finite selection and after the finitely many slopes and fields are fixed.

## 4. The precise global-depth implication and remaining gap

Suppose the H_j are critical rows of a fixed finite closed-halfspace
cover of the ORIGINAL mixed body, with mu(H_j)=beta M; other covering
rows have a fixed strict mass slack below beta M. If(P) holds, the
combined actual erosion has

 mu_e(H_j)/M_e=beta-epsilon R_j/M+o(epsilon)<beta

for every critical row. The slack rows persist and the body is nested,
so the SAME cover proves strict decrease of global normalized maximum
depth. This uses actual cover and strict positivity, not just source
membership in selected caps. It applies to oblique and supporting caps.

Nothing in(2)--(6) proves that alternative(D) is impossible at an OC
counterexample. For a specified row family it is an exact signed
boundary-integral certificate that survives EVERY action in the chosen
class. It can depend on the selected critical cover. Establishing a
favorable cover, or disproving that certificate by an actual geometric
inequality, remains additional work.

In particular, moving critical halfspaces introduce the existing min/max
branches at supporting coincidences. Additive BODY speeds do not make
those branch expressions linear, do not interchange existential inside
choices with universal outside choices, and do not turn a union of
alternative circuit covers into one convex selection problem. The
archived finite joint circuit/allocation alternative retains that order.

The new conclusion is physical closure under finite positive addition
and its exact fixed-cap response alternative. It legitimizes stronger
finite action menus, including mixtures of max-sharing actions, without
claiming their required Gamma_d/2^n payment.
